1. Capability Contract Management

Define and version a capsule's capability scope, inputs, outputs, effects, compatibility, completion conditions, and routing constraints.

2. Capsule Packaging

Bundle the capsule specification, dependencies, resources, metadata, and entry point into a loadable and distributable capability unit.

3. Capability Verification & Certification

Verify capsule schema conformance, integrity, safety, and quality requirements, then grant, update, or revoke its certification status.

4. Capsule Registry Management

Register, publish, index, version, update, and deprecate capsules while preserving ownership and lifecycle metadata.

5. Capability Discovery, Scoring & Selection

Find compatible capsules, compare them by capability, effects, quality, cost, and policy, and select the best candidate for the task.

6. Capsule Invocation

Bind inputs, context, permissions, and an execution binding to a selected capsule, invoke it, and return contract-compliant outputs and evidence.

7. Capsule Composition

Combine multiple capsules by connecting their contracts, data dependencies, effects, and failure behavior into one composite capability.

8. Capsule Evolution

Create, test, promote, migrate, or roll back new capsule versions from approved improvement proposals.

1. Operator Registration

Register a logical or physical operator with its identity, type, contract reference, owner, and initial status.

2. Operator Profile Management

Maintain the operator's role, policy, cost, risk, quota, candidate hosts, and operational metadata.

3. Operator Capability Profiling

Build an evidence-backed profile of the operator's capabilities, limitations, suitable task types, and confidence levels.

4. Operator Qualification

Check an operator's contract compliance, safety, permissions, reliability, and minimum quality before it is enabled or promoted.

5. Operator Eligibility Matching

Filter operators for a specific task using capability, policy, risk, quota, health, and host constraints.

6. Operator Selection

Rank eligible operators by quality, cost, latency, load, independence, and fallback policy, then choose the executor.

7. Operator Performance Learning

Learn task-specific success, quality, latency, cost, and failure priors from completed operator runs for future selection.

8. Operator Independence Control

Enforce separation of duties, isolation, and conflict rules between builders, evaluators, and independent reviewers.

9. Logical Operator Contract Management

Define and version stable logical work units, including their inputs, outputs, capability needs, effects, and completion conditions.

10. Logical-to-Physical Binding Eligibility

Define which logical operator and physical actor or host combinations are valid under capability, permission, and architecture rules.

11. Operator Architecture Boundary Enforcement

Prevent operators, capsules, hosts, and backends from crossing architecture layers or bypassing the shared control plane.

1. Evaluation Contract Management

Compile and version acceptance criteria, metrics, evidence requirements, thresholds, and verdict formats into an evaluation contract.

2. Evaluation Method Selection

Choose suitable static checks, tests, benchmarks, model reviews, or human reviews for the evaluation target and risk.

3. Evaluator Assignment

Assign qualified evaluators while enforcing independence, conflict-of-interest, and separation-of-duty requirements.

4. Reasoning & External Plausibility Verification

Check reasoning consistency, claim-to-evidence support, and whether the result conflicts with credible external knowledge or baselines.

5. Evaluation Calibration

Calibrate evaluator scores, thresholds, bias, and confidence using reference cases, historical errors, and reviewer agreement.

6. Evidence Admissibility & Sufficiency Gating

Check whether evidence has an acceptable type and source and sufficiently covers the evaluation contract before a verdict is allowed.

7. Human Review Gate Management

Prepare review materials, collect attributable human decisions and reasons, and manage the lifecycle of human-required gates.

8. Evaluation Verdict Generation

Aggregate evaluation results into a pass, fail, blocked, or inconclusive verdict with reasons, confidence, and required follow-up.

9. Evaluation Quality Learning

Track evaluator errors, drift, consistency, and feedback to improve later evaluator assignment and calibration.

10. Lifecycle, Parity & Runtime Claim Evaluation

Use typed evidence to verify lifecycle completion, semantic or feature parity, and claims that real execution or side effects occurred.

11. Operator Contract & Boundary Validation

Run contract, input/output, effect, smoke, and architecture-boundary checks before an operator is trusted by the system.

1. Model Capability Registry

Record declared and verified model capabilities such as modality, context size, tool use, structured output, cost class, and suitable tasks.

2. Model Routing & Selection

Match and select a model route using task needs, capability, quality, cost, policy, quota, and current health.

3. Model Context Preparation

Assemble, retrieve, compress, format, and budget the prompt and context required for a model call.

4. Model Invocation

Execute model requests through a common interface and handle streaming, timeouts, retries, and call-level errors.

5. Model Tool-Use Mediation

Control which tools a model can see, validate tool arguments, authorize calls, return results, and manage tool-use loops.

6. Model Response Normalization

Convert provider-specific text, structured output, tool calls, usage data, and errors into one standard response format.

7. Model Continuity Management

Preserve task context, continuation state, and tool state across calls, sessions, model switches, and recovery.

8. Model Availability & Fallback Management

Monitor model and provider availability and perform fallback or failover during outages, throttling, quota exhaustion, or authentication failure.

9. Model Policy Enforcement

Apply privacy, security, data-residency, budget, and allowed-use policies before and during model calls.

10. Model Usage Auditing

Record model calls, routes, users, tokens, cost, quota consumption, and policy decisions for audit and accounting.

11. Model/Provider Runtime Configuration

Resolve and provide effective endpoint, deployment, timeout, quota, default, and provider-specific settings to the runtime.

12. Model Performance Monitoring

Monitor model latency, throughput, error rate, task success, output quality, and performance regression trends.

1. Improvement Experience Capture

Collect cross-run failures, gate rejections, human interventions, poor bindings, runtime errors, and reusable success evidence.

2. Improvement Pattern Discovery

Find recurring failures, regressions, bottlenecks, and generalizable success patterns across accumulated experience.

3. Improvement Opportunity Formation

Turn a validated pattern into a scoped improvement opportunity with goals, expected benefit, risks, and supporting evidence.

4. Improvement Candidate Generation

Generate comparable changes to workflows, prompts, capsules, routing, schemas, gates, adapters, or memory policy.

5. Improvement Experimentation

Test system-change candidates through replay, A/B comparison, canary runs, or sandbox experiments.

6. Improvement Evaluation

Compare candidate effects on quality, cost, latency, reliability, and safety, then produce adoption or rejection evidence.

7. Improvement Deployment Control

Apply approved improvements through staged promotion, monitoring, version control, and rollback.

8. Improvement Policy Calibration

Adjust RSI triggers, risk levels, experiment budgets, approval requirements, and automation boundaries from long-term results.

1. Unified Data Access

Provide one addressing, reading, and query interface across structured data, documents, graphs, vectors, and artifacts.

2. Source Connector Management

Register, configure, monitor, update, and retire connectors for files, websites, research services, repositories, and other sources.

3. Source Acquisition & Structural Normalization

Acquire source content through connectors and convert it into canonical data or document structures while preserving provenance.

4. Data Quality Validation & Remediation

Detect and handle missing, corrupted, duplicated, malformed, inconsistent, or unsuccessfully normalized data.

5. Data Semantics & Schema Management

Manage field and entity semantics, ontologies, schemas, versions, compatibility, and structural validation.

6. Data Lineage & Provenance Management

Record and verify source, transformation, version, and responsibility links from original data to derived assets.

7. Hybrid Retrieval

Combine lexical, vector, graph, metadata, and filtered retrieval into ranked results with source references and scores.

8. Research Knowledge Graph Management

Manage research entities and relationships across papers, concepts, methods, claims, experiments, people, and citations.

9. Opportunity Graph Management

Manage relationships among problems, requirements, gaps, opportunities, ideas, evidence, and decisions.

10. Opportunity Metadata Enrichment

Add source, topic, impact, feasibility, risk, evidence coverage, and lifecycle metadata to opportunities.

11. Evidence Ledger Management

Record evidence identity, producer, provenance, supported claims or criteria, status, and audit history for each run.

12. Research Asset Repository

Store, version, identify, and retrieve research code, data, models, documents, figures, and experiment outputs.

13. Failure Knowledge Repository

Preserve failed attempts, counterexamples, invalid hypotheses, root causes, fixes, and recurrence conditions for later reuse.

14. Technical Memory Management

Write, compress, retrieve, expire, and govern durable technical facts, decisions, constraints, and reusable context across runs.

15. Data Governance

Enforce data access, privacy, retention, licensing, sensitivity, deletion, sharing, and audit policies.

16. Evidence & Artifact Contract Storage

Store and version evidence and artifact schemas, constraints, compatibility rules, and contract metadata.

1. Run Initialization

Create the run or sprint identity, workspace, initial state, log and evidence paths, and load effective runtime configuration.

2. Work Readiness & Task Graph Scheduling

Determine node readiness from dependencies, gates, write scopes, resources, and state, then schedule runnable work.

3. Execution Assignment, Queueing & Dispatch

Assign ready work to selected executors, manage queue order, and submit dispatch requests.

4. Execution Environment Provisioning

Prepare worktrees, sandboxes, processes, remote environments, runtime dependencies, and execution isolation.

5. Execution Admission, Approval, Lease & Concurrency Control

Check approval, policy, and resource conditions, acquire leases atomically, and enforce concurrency, exclusion, quota, and backpressure.

6. Execution Recordkeeping

Append dispatch, start, heartbeat, result, error, retry, approval, and handoff events to the execution audit history.

7. Experiment Loop Automation

Coordinate experiment preparation, execution, collection, evaluation, repetition, and stopping conditions.

8. Run Recovery Control

Recover, retry, compensate, or safely terminate runs after interruption, worker failure, stale leases, or partial results.

9. Artifact Routing

Route artifact and evidence references to downstream nodes, ledgers, repositories, or delivery channels according to contract.

10. Run Closure Assurance

Allow a run to close only after its nodes, gates, artifacts, evidence, and parent-child states satisfy closure rules.

11. Runtime Bridge & Route Execution

Execute a chosen route through actor-host, provider, CLI, API, browser, or remote adapters and normalize results and errors.

12. Runtime State and Status Management

Maintain valid state machines, transitions, and current status projections for runs, tasks, operators, actors, and hosts.

13. Actor Host & Physical Host Management

Manage host types, instances, health, carrier metadata, lifecycle, and compatibility mappings for environments that carry actors.

14. Runtime Operator Binding Activation

Resolve a planned logical-to-physical binding into an available actor-host instance ready for lease and dispatch.

1. Compiler Profile Selection

Select an intention compiler profile from the input type, domain, task risk, and required output.

2. Intent Classification & Command Parsing

Parse natural-language or command structure and identify the intent category, action, flags, and candidate task type.

3. Goal Extraction & Parameter Binding

Extract goals, objects, success conditions, and parameters, then bind them to normalized contract fields.

4. Context Projection

Select and project the minimum relevant project, memory, attachment, and historical context needed for the intention.

5. Ambiguity Detection

Identify missing, conflicting, or ambiguous goals, terms, scope, constraints, priorities, and success conditions.

6. Clarification Generation

Generate the smallest answerable questions needed to resolve blocking ambiguity and complete the contract.

7. Constraint Compilation

Convert budget, time, permission, scope, quality, data, approval, and prohibition requirements into enforceable constraints.

8. Task Contract Compilation

Compile goals, context, constraints, and acceptance criteria into a stable and traceable task contract.

9. Contract Traceability

Link raw input, requirements, goals, constraints, task contracts, plan nodes, and acceptance evidence.

10. Execution Envelope Construction

Assemble the task contract, context, chosen binding, criticality, timeout, retry, approval, and evidence references into a dispatch envelope.

11. Approval Contract Compilation

Define who can approve which side effect or state transition, under what conditions, using what evidence, and for how long.

1. Task Decomposition

Split a task contract into bounded work units with explicit inputs, outputs, completion conditions, and responsibilities.

2. Planning Strategy Selection

Choose a sequential, parallel, iterative, exploratory, or other planning strategy from task type, risk, uncertainty, and cost.

3. Research and Experiment Planning

Create the domain-level logical plan for research, retrieval, hypotheses, experiments, benchmarks, and verification.

4. Report and Delivery Handoff Planning

Plan the creation, review, compilation, packaging, and consumer handoff of reports and delivery artifacts.

5. Dependency Graph Formation

Create and validate data, control, gate, artifact, and parent-child dependencies among planned work units.

6. Execution Requirement Compilation

Define capability, environment, tool, data, security, evidence, and side-effect requirements for every plan node.

7. Resource Planning

Estimate and allocate time, compute, model budget, concurrency, storage, equipment, and human attention.

8. Assurance Planning

Plan evaluators, tests, benchmarks, human gates, evidence, and rollback needed to prove task completion.

9. Plan Validation

Check plan coverage, dependency validity, executability, risk, and compliance with the task contract and constraints.

10. Physical Plan Selection

Compare executable topologies and resource strategies, then choose an overall physical plan with cost, risk, and fallback rationale.

11. Plan Evolution

Version and revise unfinished plans when requirements, evidence, constraints, or execution feedback change.

12. Runtime Execution Planning

Translate a domain plan into runtime batches, environments, resources, concurrency, recovery, dispatch, and fallback intentions.

13. Physical Operator Binding Planning

Select a concrete or ordered set of physical actor-host bindings for plan nodes and define their fallback ladder.

1. Build Contract Interpretation

Translate the task or build contract into implementation goals, interfaces, write scope, acceptance conditions, and prohibited changes.

2. Build Preparation

Prepare source material, dependencies, templates, data, workspace, toolchain, and pre-build readiness checks.

3. Code Construction

Create or modify deterministic source code, scripts, tests, and configuration to implement the required technical function.

4. Model Construction

Build, train, fine-tune, or assemble reproducible algorithmic, statistical, or machine-learning models.

5. Experimental Asset Construction

Build experiment code, data processing, instrumentation, environment descriptions, and run scripts.

6. Benchmark Asset Construction

Build benchmark datasets, harnesses, workloads, baselines, metric implementations, and comparison scripts.

7. Verification Asset Construction

Build unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, validators, fixtures, checklists, and verification scripts.

8. Decision Artifact Construction

Create opportunity cards, decision records, trade-off matrices, and recommendation packets for decision-making.

9. Prototype Assembly

Combine code, models, data, and interfaces into a bounded, runnable, and demonstrable proof of concept.

10. Product Integration

Integrate verified components into target product interfaces, data flows, and production-oriented operational boundaries.

11. Defect Repair

Use failure evidence to identify and repair code, configuration, contract, or integration defects and prevent regression.

12. Build Evidence Generation

Generate diffs, manifests, hashes, compile and test results, provenance, and acceptance evidence for the build.

13. Report/Paper/Deliverable Construction

Create and assemble human-facing reports, papers, slides, posters, rebuttals, and narrative delivery packages.

14. Runtime Deliverable Construction

Build executable or deployable services, packages, containers, workflow bundles, and deployment configuration.
